note: Hand-written from data/about (proposal + FAQ), then length-balanced. Review before presenting.

questions.q: Before askEd's language model writes an answer, what happens to the student's question?
options: Relevant pieces of course material are retrieved and passed to the model as context
The model is retrained overnight on the course notes so that it can recite them from memory
A teaching assistant reads the question and writes up key points for the model to use
The model runs a search across the open internet for pages resembling the question
questions.explanation: Retrieval-augmented generation finds relevant chunks first and gives them to the model, so the answer is built from real course material.

questions.q: What does it mean that an askEd answer is 'grounded'?
options: A lecturer reviews and approves every answer before the student is allowed to see it
It is built from retrieved course excerpts and names the sources they came from
It is produced by fixed hand-written rules and no language model is involved at all
The model may only repeat sentences copied word for word out of the course notes
questions.explanation: Grounded answers rest on retrieved material and name their sources, rather than being invented.

questions.q: Why does askEd split course documents into small chunks with some overlap before indexing?
options: Small chunks can match a specific question, and overlap keeps ideas from being cut off
Every chunk is used to train its own separate copy of the language model afterwards
Short chunks let the database store each file without ever exceeding its size limits
Splitting means a student can only ever be shown a small fraction of each document
questions.explanation: Chunks of about 500 characters with 100 characters of overlap are small enough to match a question while keeping context across boundaries.

questions.q: askEd also indexes past staff-answered threads. What does that give it?
options: It can automatically post those older answers to the forum on the staff's behalf
It no longer needs any lecture notes because the staff answers replace them entirely
Questions staff already answered can be answered again from that stored knowledge
Students can edit the staff answers directly to keep them accurate and up to date
questions.explanation: Staff answers become searchable knowledge instead of being lost when the thread scrolls away; askEd itself never posts.

questions.q: A student asks about something that is not in the indexed material. What should askEd do?
options: Post the question on the forum so that a classmate can write a reply in its place
Return the closest passage it found even when that passage has nothing to do with it
Say that the answer is not in the material it was given, rather than guessing
Fall back on general knowledge and present the result as an official course answer
questions.explanation: If nothing relevant is found, askEd declines rather than inventing an answer.

questions.q: What does the confidence figure shown next to an askEd answer actually represent?
options: How certain the underlying model is that the retrieved information will satisfy the student's understanding
The percentage of similar questions where this answer has been used successfully by other students
How closely the best retrieved passage matched the question, which is not the chance the answer is right
The probability that the answer directly addresses the student's specific learning need, based on question difficulty
questions.explanation: It is the similarity of the best retrieved chunk. It is not a calibrated probability of correctness.

questions.q: Why is askEd's output labelled an AI preview and not an official answer?
options: Only the student who asked can read it, and it expires as soon as the thread closes
EdStem requires every automated reply to carry a badge saying it is only a preview
Staff have not checked it, and its factual accuracy has not been formally evaluated
The text is deliberately shortened and staff keep the full version for themselves
questions.explanation: The label keeps staff in control; accuracy has not been formally measured.

questions.q: Discarding weak retrieval matches mainly reduces which risk?
options: Students being shown answers that earlier cohorts wrote about the same topic
Fluent answers that sound convincing but are only loosely backed by course material
Slow replies caused by searching through too many documents at the same moment
Staff accidentally deleting threads while the assistant happens to be running
questions.explanation: Matches that are not similar enough are dropped, so the model is not asked to build on weak evidence.

questions.q: Which statement about question text and AI providers is true for askEd?
options: The provider is automatically subject to the same privacy regulations as the institution
Question text is stored locally in the student's browser cache so the provider never receives it
Only anonymized metadata about the question is sent to the provider, not the actual content
Question text is sent to the configured model provider, so real use needs institutional sign-off
questions.explanation: Third-party processing of question text is a named privacy risk that needs institutional approval.

questions.q: What does it mean that askEd is 'read-only' on EdStem?
options: It can read only those threads that staff have already marked as answered
It can read threads but never posts, edits or deletes anything on the forum
It can edit its own earlier replies but cannot touch anyone else's posts
It can post replies, but only after a teaching assistant approves each one
questions.explanation: askEd never writes to EdStem, so staff keep full control of what gets posted.

questions.q: Why must the local lecturer dashboard not be exposed on the public internet?
options: The prototype has no login, so anyone who could reach it would see the analytics
Visitors could overwrite the course notes that the assistant has indexed
It is built for one viewer at a time and crashes when several people connect
Public traffic would use up the language model quota within a few minutes
questions.explanation: The local dashboard has no authentication, which is why this public demo does not expose it.

questions.q: In tonight's live demo, what happens to the questions you submit?
options: They are sent directly to the instructor's inbox as individual messages with your student ID
They are saved with your name attached and shared with all other students in the course
They are displayed one at a time on the presenter screen and then immediately deleted from the system
They are stored anonymously in the deployment's database and counted by topic on the presenter screen
questions.explanation: Audience questions are anonymous, stored in the deployment's database, and only aggregate counts are projected.

questions.q: How does the askEd bot find out about new questions on a course?
options: A scheduled job uploads a complete export of the forum once every single day
It listens to the course's live event stream and backfills recent threads
A teaching assistant forwards each new question to it by email as it arrives
Students must submit questions through a separate form that askEd provides
questions.explanation: It uses EdStem's WebSocket stream for live events and the REST API to backfill recent questions, read-only.

questions.q: What does askEd do with each new question it sees?
options: It categorizes the question by difficulty level and routes it to the most qualified teaching assistant
It compares the question to a database of frequently asked questions and suppresses duplicates
It searches the internet for similar questions and returns the top results to the student
It matches the question against course material and tags it with one or more of 15 topics
questions.explanation: Each question is retrieved against, classified into Computer Systems topics, and logged for the dashboard.

questions.q: Who sees the Chrome extension's answer preview, and where does it appear?
options: Everyone viewing the thread, inserted directly into the original question post
Only instructors, displayed in a separate admin dashboard outside the forum
The student and staff, shown in a collapsible section at the top of the thread page
Only the student, in a panel on the thread page, without changing the thread itself
questions.explanation: The panel is added to the page in the student's browser; nothing is posted to EdStem.

questions.q: Which statement about askEd's relationship with EdStem is accurate?
options: It is a separate tool that EdStem does not run or endorse, and it depends on EdStem's API
It is an official EdStem product that the company developed and actively supports
EdStem integrates askEd directly into its platform and monitors all of its responses
It is a third-party tool that EdStem operates independently from its main infrastructure
questions.explanation: askEd is independent, so students should be told it is optional and not endorsed by EdStem.

questions.q: What can a student do with the askEd Chrome extension on a thread?
options: Request an AI answer preview with sources, or take a short multiple-choice quiz
Rate other students' answers and push the best ones to the top of the page
Have the assistant write and submit their reply to the thread on their behalf
Download the full set of course notes for the thread's topic as a single file
questions.explanation: The extension offers a cited answer preview and a short self-test quiz.

questions.q: What is sent to the AI model when a student first loads an EdStem thread?
options: A hashed copy of the student's account name, so replies can be personalised
The thread title only, so the model can pre-load a likely answer
Nothing, because the question is only used once the student opens the panel
The full thread including every reply, so the answer is ready in advance
questions.explanation: No model call happens until the panel is first expanded.

questions.q: What is claimed about the answer preview's effect on near-duplicate questions?
options: It has been shown to cut the number of duplicate questions roughly in half
It removes the need for teaching assistants to monitor the forum at all
It is aimed at reducing them, but that effect has not been measured yet
It makes no real difference and was added mainly to look more impressive
questions.explanation: The benefit is an intention and expectation; no workload or learning outcome has been evaluated.

questions.q: What is the quiz in the extension for?
options: Providing personalized topic recommendations based on each student's performance patterns
Self-testing on the thread's topic, with instant feedback and an explanation for each answer
Determining whether the student has sufficient knowledge to view the full thread discussion
Generating a score that is recorded in the student's official transcript
questions.explanation: The extension quiz is a low-stakes self-test with immediate feedback.

questions.q: What does a high question count for a topic on the dashboard indicate?
options: That students lack understanding of the topic and need remedial instruction
Insufficient coverage of that topic during the lecture session
A direct correlation between question count and student performance on that topic
Interest or concern in that topic, which is not necessarily confusion
questions.explanation: Question frequency shows interest or concern, not necessarily confusion, and is not a measure of learning.

questions.q: What ends up in the dashboard's 'needs review' queue?
options: Answers that have been viewed by more than five different users without any staff interaction
Topics that appear in the knowledge base but were not successfully matched to any student question
Questions that contain multiple choice options or require numerical calculations
Questions that were answered with low confidence or could not be sorted into a topic
questions.explanation: Low-confidence or unclassified questions are queued so staff can spot gaps in coverage.

questions.q: How might a course organiser use the topic trends at mid-term?
options: To identify which topics students found easy and remove them from future assessments
To see which topics drew the most questions and decide what to revisit or re-explain
To determine which students asked too many questions and need independent study instead
To calculate how much each topic should count toward the final grade based on question frequency
questions.explanation: Topic distribution and trends give an evidence base for what to revisit before the next cohort.

questions.q: What day-to-day use of the dashboard is described for TAs?
options: Filtering spam and removing inappropriate messages from the discussion forum
Reviewing individual student questions to provide personalized feedback on each post
Tracking student engagement metrics to identify who needs intervention support
Spotting repeated questions so they can act once, for example by pinning an answer
questions.explanation: Seeing recurring questions lets TAs fix them once rather than re-answering each time.

questions.q: Which statement describes askEd's scalability today?
options: It runs as a single instance and has not been load tested at scale
It needs a cluster of specialised processors in order to run at all
It automatically spreads across many servers as demand grows
It has been tested with thousands of students using it simultaneously
questions.explanation: The prototype is one FastAPI instance, with in-memory limits, and no load testing at scale.

questions.q: What does 'LLM-provider agnostic' mean for askEd?
options: It is limited to using whichever provider has the most up-to-date models available
It operates independently without relying on any external language model provider at all
The language model can be switched between OpenAI, Gemini or Claude by configuration
The language model automatically rotates between OpenAI, Gemini, and Claude on each query to balance usage
questions.explanation: One interface hides provider differences, so a department is not locked into one vendor.

questions.q: Where can askEd run?
options: Locally on a laptop, or on a hosting service such as the one used for this live demo
Only through a web browser without any local installation, because it cannot run offline
Only on a university server, because the AI models are too large for personal computers
Only on a cloud platform like AWS or Azure, because it requires distributed computing infrastructure
questions.explanation: It is a FastAPI service that can run locally or on a host such as Render.

questions.q: What limits the quality of askEd's answers on a new course?
options: Staff must first retype every document into a special proprietary format
It can only read materials that were written in English by a single author
What has been ingested, and scanned PDFs without a text layer index poorly
Nothing, because it answers any subject equally well whatever has been loaded
questions.explanation: Answer quality depends on the ingested material and on how well text can be extracted from PDFs.

questions.q: What has been measured about askEd's effect on learning or TA workload so far?
options: A large reduction in TA workload across several different courses
A modest gain in exam marks for students who used the preview
Only student satisfaction, which was reported as very high
Nothing yet, because those outcomes have not been evaluated
questions.explanation: No learning gains, workload reduction or answer accuracy have been measured; benefits are expectations.

questions.q: Which risk is named about students using AI previews?
options: Previews making the forum load too slowly for anyone to use it properly
Over-reliance, where students stop engaging with staff or with their peers
Students being charged a small fee for every preview that they request
Previews revealing other students' private questions to the whole class
questions.explanation: Over-reliance is one of the named risks; visible confidence and encouraging posting are the mitigations.

questions.q: Why might askEd's picture of the 'difficult topics' be distorted?
options: Under-covered topics get worse answers and tagging, which skews the picture
Every page view on the forum is counted as if it were a separate question
It only counts questions that were asked by members of the teaching staff
The list of topics is reshuffled at random every single week of the term
questions.explanation: Bias in classification and coverage could distort the mid-term view; the needs-review queue helps catch it.

questions.q: What is suggested for monitoring after widespread use?
options: Whether the vector database grows beyond the storage quota it has been given
Whether students ask peers fewer questions because the AI preview satisfies them
Whether teaching assistants stop using the EdStem platform for any purpose
Whether the assistant starts to write its own exam questions without being asked
questions.explanation: Widespread use could shift question-asking behaviour, which the analytics can monitor.
